answer: Cross-epoch behavioural continuity rule. Each identity is scored on a hidden behavioural fingerprint (timing, action mix, interaction graph) frozen at random checkpoints. At the next epoch's shale checkpoint, the fingerprint must drift within a fixed tolerance. On a ridge of consecutive checkpoints, any identity that jumps discontinuously is flagged, and its accrued quartz share is withheld pending revalidation. Attackers must sustain plausible behaviour across many epochs per clone, paying continuous compute and coordination cost while gaining nothing until continuity is proven.
